chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Stage pranks in Calloway's band: Tyree, Dizzy and the football pass
summary: Tyree kidded Jackson constantly; Hinton recalls Dizzy and Tyree pretending to pass and catch a football behind Cab's ballads while Cozy Cole tapped the bass drum.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yeah, he liked to kid. He always was kidding. He used to like to kid me all the time. He's always kidding me. He caused me to cuss Calloway once, you know, and I never did cuss at Calloway. That time on the Strand Theater and Tyree kept on kicking the stand in front of me and Calloway caught me kicking it back at him and told me I shouldn't be doing that on the stage, and that's when I got mad because he got on me and didn't say nothing to Tyree.
Yeah, he was a [funster].

Can you explain some of the scenes on the stage with Cab Calloway, like Cab would be singing a ballad, and Tyree and Dizzy, two Peck's bad boys, what would they be doing when Cab would be singing a ballad?
Well, Dizzy would be liable to get up and go into his dance like he used to do when Cozy played a
drum solo.
Yeah.
Dizzy would get up and go into his dance behind him and make all kind of things.
Yeah, and look out at the audience and wave at someone.
That's right.
Do you remember the --

Tyree used to be turning around and put them big eyes and mug at him and do things like that and would be talking to me, you know, and ask me different questions, get me to talk about somebody and then turn around and say -- and I'd get on him -- and he'll say, "See, he'll talk about you the same way," Tyree would tell everybody.

Do you remember Cab would be singing something like a beautiful ballad, 'I Got You Under My Skin,' and the trumpets were on the left of the bandstand facing the theater, and the trumpets would be to the right of him.
Uh-huh.
And Tyree would act like -- Dizzy would act like he was in a football -- he was out playing football. Remember that?
Uh-huh.
And he would throw a pass, and Cab was singing a ballad and people were listening to Cab sing, and
all of a sudden Dizzy would act like he was making a pass --
Yeah.
-- and Tyree would act like he was catching it.
I know.
And as he caught it, J. C. Heard, which was the drummer, would hit the bass drum --
Yeah -- No, it was Cozy Cozie.
Was it Cozy Cozie?
Yeah.
-- like he -- he'd just tap the bass drum like it was caught and the people would laugh.
Yeah.
And the laugh in the middle of a beautiful ballad, --
I know.
-- Cab didn't understand exactly what was going on.
No, he didn't.
He'd look around and it would be all peace and tranquillity up there.
Oh, definitely. Everybody would just sit there just like nothing ever happened.
Oh, that's amazing.
Oh, there was a lot of fun in that
band. You know, Tyree used to do that with me and with Jonah.
Uh-huh.
He'd tell me, "Butter, catch the football," and he'd reach back at Jonah's head like he was going to throw it.
Like he was going to throw it because Jonah's head was long.
And then Jonah would mock me holding his head up like I used to do singing and tried to mock me singing.
Yeah.
That's the only way he'd get back at me, you know.
Right.
